summary: AgroCycle IA is an artificial intelligence-based agricultural platform created to help producers adapt to climate change by transforming complex satellite, climate, and soil data into simple, practical recommendations for crop rotation, water management, and field planning. Its core objective is to build a more resilient, sustainable, and economically viable agricultural sector, mitigating the impacts of droughts, irregular rainfall, and soil degradation while increasing productivity, reducing crop losses, and promoting efficient water use. Developed with the support of artificial intelligences such as Gemini, Claude, and ChatGPT during the prototyping, programming, and refinement stages, the solution integrates cutting-edge technologies and scientific databases—including the NASA POWER Agroclimatology API, NASA SMAP, SoilGrids v2.0, Open-Meteo, and ESRI World Imagery—to deliver an accessible, scalable, and effective tool for food security and environmental preservation.
details:
AgroCycle AI is an agricultural platform based on artificial intelligence that helps farmers adapt to climate change by analyzing satellite, climate, and soil data from sources such as NASA. The system provides forecasts and recommendations for crop rotation, water management, and agricultural planning, assisting producers in making better-informed decisions and reducing risks stemming from extreme weather conditions.
The project offers several benefits, including increased productivity, reduced crop losses, more efficient water use, and improved soil conservation. By leveraging real-time environmental data and artificial intelligence, AgroCycle AI enables farmers to optimize resources and adopt more sustainable agricultural practices.
The core objective of the project is to create a more resilient and sustainable agricultural sector. The platform seeks to mitigate the impacts of droughts, irregular rainfall, and soil degradation, while simultaneously supporting food security and environmental preservation.
To develop this solution, the team integrated technologies such as the NASA POWER Agroclimatology API, NASA SMAP, the SoilGrids v2.0 REST API, the Open-Meteo Agricultural Forecast API, and ESRI World Imagery. These tools provide the environmental and agricultural data necessary to generate forecasts and recommendations. It is worth noting that the concept was developed with the assistance of artificial intelligence—specifically Gemini, Google Cloud, and ChatGPT—which supported prototyping, programming, and the refinement of the idea.
The key differentiator of AgroCycle AI lies in its ability to transform complex scientific and satellite data into simple, actionable insights for farmers. The team took into account fundamental challenges—such as climate change, water scarcity, soil quality, sustainability, economic viability, and future scalability—ensuring that the solution remains accessible and effective for producers.
